title: Batching profile candidates (SLO tiers) — working sheet
content:
Spreadsheet-style working doc used to pick initial default knob sets for the three SLO tiers (fast / standard / cost-efficient). Values below are *candidate scheduler caps* (not hard guarantees) and are evaluated via benchmark-lab mixed-workload suite.

Legend / columns
- max_batch_tokens: cap on total tokens admitted into a batch window (prefill+decode), scheduler-side
- max_wait_ms: batch window wait time budget before dispatch (per stage; see notes)
- prefill:decode split: intended scheduler weighting between prefill and decode work when both are queued (implemented as dynamic quotas; expressed as target share)
- streaming metrics: TTFT (time-to-first-token) and p99 inter-token gap (ITG) proxy
- non-streaming metrics: E2E latency for fixed output length (benchmark uses 256 output tokens unless noted)
- throughput: output tokens/sec per GPU (median during steady-state)
- cost delta: relative $/1K tokens estimate vs Jan baseline profile for the same model+HW (uses internal metering; excludes idle)

Assumed test harness (current)
- Workload mix: 40% chat (streaming), 35% summarization (non-stream), 25% code (mixed)
- Prompt length distribution (tokens): p50=420, p90=1,400, p99=6,000 (mixture across tasks)
- Concurrency ramp: 4 → 64 in steps; report values at 32 concurrency unless otherwise stated
- Regions: us-east (primary), eu-west spot-check; numbers below are us-east unless marked
- Hardware classes in sheet: H100-80GB (hosted), A100-80GB (dedicated common), L40S-48GB (cost-focused pools)

PASS/FAIL gates (summary; see SLO tier doc for full)
- FAST: streaming TTFT p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms; non-stream E2E p95 <= 1.8s; no starvation events in 30-min soak
- STANDARD: streaming TTFT p95 <= 450ms; non-stream E2E p95 <= 2.8s; queue depth p99 bounded under burst
- COST-EFFICIENT: maintain correctness; non-stream E2E p95 <= 4.5s; streaming TTFT p95 <= 700ms; prevent queue blowups (shed at configured threshold)

=============================
CANDIDATE PROFILES (v0.7)
=============================

Table 1 — Candidate knob sets (by tier/model family/HW)

| profile_id | tier | model_family | hw_class | max_batch_tokens | max_wait_ms | prefill:decode split | notes |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| F-H100-L3-01 | fast | llama3-70b | H100-80GB | 4096 | 1.2 | 60:40 | tight wait; decode gets protected quota to avoid ITG spikes |
| F-A100-L3-01 | fast | llama3-70b | A100-80GB | 3072 | 1.0 | 65:35 | A100 decode sensitive; keep batches smaller; admission control triggers earlier |
| F-H100-MX8-01 | fast | mixtral-8x7b | H100-80GB | 6144 | 1.5 | 55:45 | higher prefill cap ok; avoid large decode batches to protect tail |
| S-H100-L3-01 | standard | llama3-70b | H100-80GB | 8192 | 2.5 | 55:45 | default for hosted if no tier chosen (tentative) |
| S-A100-L3-01 | standard | llama3-70b | A100-80GB | 6144 | 2.0 | 60:40 | safe baseline for Dedicated clusters |
| S-L40S-L31-01 | standard | llama3.1-8b | L40S-48GB | 8192 | 3.0 | 50:50 | smaller model; leverage batching to reduce $/token |
| C-H100-L3-01 | cost-efficient | llama3-70b | H100-80GB | 16384 | 6.0 | 50:50 | aggressive; relies on overload guardrails + shed thresholds |
| C-A100-L3-01 | cost-efficient | llama3-70b | A100-80GB | 12288 | 6.5 | 55:45 | A100 needs slightly more prefill share to avoid queue inversion |
| C-L40S-L31-01 | cost-efficient | llama3.1-8b | L40S-48GB | 24576 | 8.0 | 45:55 | maximize throughput; decode share bumped to reduce ITG regressions |
| F-H100-QW-01 | fast | qwen2.5-72b | H100-80GB | 4096 | 1.3 | 60:40 | similar to L3-70B; watch TTFT at long prompts |
| S-H100-QW-01 | standard | qwen2.5-72b | H100-80GB | 8192 | 2.8 | 55:45 | stable; good utilization at mid prompts |
| C-H100-QW-01 | cost-efficient | qwen2.5-72b | H100-80GB | 16384 | 6.5 | 50:50 | needs strict backpressure at high concurrency |

Table 2 — Benchmark summary (steady-state @ concurrency=32; mixed workload)

| profile_id | streaming TTFT p50/p95/p99 (ms) | streaming ITG p99 (ms) | non-stream E2E p50/p95 (ms) | throughput tok/s/GPU | queue depth p99 | cost delta vs baseline |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| F-H100-L3-01 | 120 / 235 / 410 | 78 | 980 / 1680 | 1,720 | 14 | -6% |
| F-A100-L3-01 | 135 / 248 / 445 | 92 | 1,120 / 1,790 | 1,180 | 18 | -4% |
| F-H100-MX8-01 | 110 / 220 / 395 | 74 | 860 / 1,520 | 2,050 | 12 | -7% |
| S-H100-L3-01 | 150 / 380 / 690 | 110 | 1,050 / 2,520 | 2,320 | 28 | -14% |
| S-A100-L3-01 | 165 / 410 / 760 | 125 | 1,210 / 2,740 | 1,610 | 35 | -12% |
| S-L40S-L31-01 | 140 / 360 / 640 | 118 | 780 / 2,050 | 3,900 | 22 | -18% |
| C-H100-L3-01 | 210 / 620 / 1,120 | 180 | 1,280 / 3,980 | 3,050 | 64 | -23% |
| C-A100-L3-01 | 235 / 680 / 1,260 | 210 | 1,420 / 4,260 | 2,080 | 78 | -21% |
| C-L40S-L31-01 | 260 / 720 / 1,380 | 240 | 980 / 3,850 | 5,600 | 70 | -27% |
| F-H100-QW-01 | 125 / 245 / 430 | 82 | 1,020 / 1,730 | 1,650 | 16 | -5% |
| S-H100-QW-01 | 160 / 405 / 740 | 116 | 1,110 / 2,640 | 2,260 | 30 | -13% |
| C-H100-QW-01 | 220 / 660 / 1,240 | 195 | 1,330 / 4,120 | 2,980 | 68 | -22% |

Notes / caveats on the numbers
- All runs use the same kernel build + quantization settings as baseline; this sheet is isolating batching/scheduler knobs.
- Streaming ITG p99 is a proxy derived from token timestamps in the harness; it is sensitive to client-side buffering. Treat deltas as directional.
- Queue depth p99 is “requests pending admission” per GPU worker; during overload mode we expect higher values but require bounded growth.

=============================
ANOMALIES / INVESTIGATIONS
=============================
- Fast tier p99 regression (llama3-70b, A100): seen when prompt length > 4k and concurrency > 48; hypothesized decode quota starvation when prefill bursts occur. Proposed mitigation: min decode reservation + earlier admission control (tracked in runtime PR-28458 follow-ups).
- Cost-efficient queue blowups: if max_wait_ms > 8ms on H100-L3 with high variance prompts, tail increases sharply and shed triggers too late. Current guardrail: shed when (queue_depth > 80) OR (estimated_wait > 2x tier budget).
- L40S cost-efficient: highest throughput wins but streaming quality is borderline for “standard”; recommend defaulting L40S pools to standard unless explicitly cost-efficient.

=============================
RECOMMENDATION (CURRENT)
=============================
- Default tier for Hosted API (when unspecified): STANDARD profiles (S-H100-L3-01 / S-H100-QW-01) + model-family mapping.
- Dedicated: default STANDARD; allow per-tenant override to FAST for streaming-heavy workloads; require explicit opt-in for COST-EFFICIENT until we have more soak time.
- COST-EFFICIENT: ship with stricter overload mode + explicit reason codes when shedding or switching profiles.

=============================
NEXT UPDATES / TODO
=============================
- Add per-prompt-length bucket breakdown (0–256, 256–1k, 1k–4k, 4k+) for TTFT and E2E; current aggregates are hiding worst-case p99 for long prompts.
- Add “mixed streaming+non-streaming on same worker” scenario (perf-suite task from ENG-18427) and re-run FAST tier gates.
- Record “prefill spikes” metric and correlate with ITG regressions for FAST.
- Re-run eu-west for S-H100-L3-01 and C-H100-L3-01 before launch brief sign-off.

Change log
- 2026-03-28: updated cost-efficient wait budgets; added qwen2.5-72b rows; refreshed numbers after benchmark-lab/pr-612 merge.
- 2026-03-14: introduced L40S profiles for 8B class; added queue depth p99.
- 2026-02-06: initial v0.3 table with llama3-70b H100/A100 only.
